items.note: Matches ESC 2021 diuretic algorithm: under-dosed first bolus, output ~63 mL/h, so double the IV loop dose; B the only defensible answer. Option C wording slightly loose. From knowledge.
ESC 2023 IE: TOE is class I with a prosthetic valve and after a negative TTE; key unambiguous, distractors are each right one step later. On the easy side for an internist.
ESC 2023 ACS very-high-risk criteria (refractory pain, recurrent dynamic ST change) correctly keyed to under 2 h; stem realistic and tests a common, consequential misreading of 'stable'.
Coherent, realistic first-diagnosed AF; results fit; key correct on ESC 2024 (CHA2DS2-VA 3, 24 h window), apixaban 5 mg with one criterion, CrCl ~31, aspirin stopped. Good numeric trap.

feedback.note: Grades right; rules and thresholds accurate and correctly attributed (ESC 2021 HF, DOSE, ESC 2023 IE/ACS, IIa downgrade); open about unverified sources. 'Little extra natriuresis' a bit strong.
Fair grading; apixaban, 24 h window, RACE II and EAST-AFNET 4 figures correct. Quibbles: EAST CI is 96% not 95%; ESC 2024 points cited via a secondary summary; 'bradycardia and falls' is rhetoric.
Conceded what did not change care (score, window) and held the dose and angiography timing on patient-impact grounds; proportionate, but brief and no source re-check or citation.

quality.note: Accurate, current ESC-based items at the right pitch for internal medicine, with fair grading and feedback aimed at the deciding criterion; only minor citation and wording quibbles.
concerns: Final feedback: EAST-AFNET 4 hazard ratio interval was a 96% CI in the paper, reported as 95%.
Final feedback: ESC 2024 AF recommendations are cited through an ACC summary, and the 24-hour window from memory (stated); correct as far as I know, but worth a primary citation.
Q1 option C ('same daily dose' as infusion) does not say which dose; harmless but could be tightened.
Scorer note: web searches returned links only, so accuracy was judged from knowledge rather than re-read primary text.
